deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of the opening of Part II of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). The previous page sets up the n-sheeted surface T over the z-plane for an irreducible F(s,z)=0. This page goes from the algebraic functions to their integrals and to the topological preparation for them.

(a) Programme (top, heavily struck). Riemann considers functions on T whose different continuations over the same part of T differ only by additive constants. These are Abelian integrals w, with dw single-valued on T. Rather than obtaining them by integrating rational functions of (s,z), he announces that he will define them by the Dirichlet principle, through boundary and discontinuity conditions ('durch Grenz- und Unstetigkeitsbedingungen definiren'). A system of algebraic functions with the same branching (Verzweigungsart) as T is mentioned as the class being treated.

(b) Parity of the number of cross-cuts. The surface T is n-sheeted over the whole plane and, by the previous page, may be regarded as closed. It is cut into a simply connected surface T* (also written T'). The page's argument, with the implicit steps filled by me:
- A simply connected surface has a boundary consisting of exactly one piece.
- The closed surface is first cut by a closed cut (Rückkehrschnitt). This yields 2 boundary pieces.
- Every further cross-cut changes the number of boundary pieces by +1 or -1.
- Hence after the first closed cut, an even number of further cuts leaves an even number of boundary pieces, and an odd number leaves an odd number.
- Reaching a single boundary piece therefore needs an odd number of further cuts, so the total number of cuts is even. Riemann sets it equal to 2p.
- In modern terms: start with χ = 2-2p. A closed cut leaves χ unchanged. Each of the 2p-1 subsequent arc cuts raises χ by 1, giving χ = 1, a disc.

(c) Normalisation of the cut system. 'Zur Vereinfachung' every later cut is drawn from a point of an earlier cut to the corresponding point on the other side of that cut. The result is a single connected cut system whose two banks together form the one boundary of T*.

(d) Constancy of the jump (periods). Several attempts are made, culminating in the final sentence, which is essentially the published text. Let a quantity w be continuous along the whole boundary of T'. Suppose it changes by equal amounts on both banks, i.e. dw+ = dw- along the cuts. Then the difference w+ - w- of its two values at the same point of the cut system is constant along every part of a cross-cut. Proof (implicit): d(w+ - w-) = dw+ - dw- = 0 along the cut. These constants are the moduli of periodicity of the Abelian integral, one per cross-cut, 2p in all.
errors: No mathematical errors. The parity argument is stated elliptically, and the first closed (return) cut that produces two boundary pieces is implicit rather than stated in the legible text.
Notation wavers between T* and T' for the cut surface, as is common in Riemann's drafts. The published text uses T'.

results.what: A closed Riemann surface is made simply connected by an even number 2p of cross-cuts. p is the genus, and the connectivity is 2p+1.
results.modern_name: Canonical dissection of a closed surface of genus p; first Betti number 2p

results.what: Arrangement of the cuts so that each later cut runs from a point of an earlier cut to the corresponding point on its other bank.
results.modern_name: Canonical cut system / fundamental polygon (a_i, b_i curves)

results.what: If dw is the same on both banks of the cut system, the jump w+ - w- is constant along each cross-cut.
results.modern_name: Periods of Abelian integrals (moduli of periodicity)

results.what: Definition of Abelian integrals by boundary and discontinuity conditions via the Dirichlet principle.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of passages that appear almost verbatim in the published 1857 paper (Part II, section 1). Only the drafting process is new.

checkable.asserts: One closed cut (χ unchanged) followed by 2p-1 arc cuts (each raising χ by 1) turns a closed genus-p surface (χ=2-2p) into a disc (χ=1). So 2p cuts in total.
Parity: starting from 2 boundary pieces with ±1 per cut, reaching 1 piece needs an odd number k of further cuts, so the total 1+k is even.

checkable.sympy: x=symbols('x'); f=Function('f'); c=symbols('c'); diff((f(x)+c) - f(x), x) == 0
checkable.asserts: If the two bank values differ only by a constant (equal increments on both banks), their difference has zero derivative along the cut.

transcription_corrections: 'Es sei nun die ... allenthalben einfach zusammenhängende[?] ... Fläche T' is probably 'die der z-Ebene allenthalben n-fach ausgebreitete' (as on the previous page). 'Einfach zusammenhängend' contradicts the subsequent cutting into a simply connected T*.
'denselben Punkte' in the final sentence should read 'demselben Punkte'.

The parity sentence should read roughly: 'eine geschlossene Fläche durch einen Rückkehrschnitt in eine Fläche mit zwei Begrenzungsstücken ... durch eine gerade Anzahl von Schnitten eine gerade, durch eine ungerade eine ungerade Zahl von Begrenzungsstücken erhält'.
'Abelschen Functionen[?]' in the margin before 'Es sei nun' is likely a section heading or catchword ('Vorbereitung'/'Abel'sche Functionen'). It is uncertain.
The cut surface is written both T* and T'. Both appear in the image.
